name: Footwear manufacturing
shape_facts: Product type: formal, casual, sports, school, safety, sandals/chappals, traditional ( khussa, Peshawari).
Made-to-stock for dealers/retail, made-to-order for brands/export, or own retail.
Pairs per day roughly, and number of sizes and colours per article.
Which processes are in-house (cutting, closing, sole moulding, lasting) vs bought or outsourced.
Sales channels: dealers, own shops, Daraz/online, institutions (schools, factories).
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: broken size sets, slow-moving articles, sole and material shortages, mould and machine downtime, defects and returns, dealer credit and collections, and production visibility. pi does not advise on safety-footwear certification or standards, chemical or adhesive handling, orthopaedic or medical fit claims, customs or taxes. pi records roles and dealer types, not names or IDs.

vocabulary.upper: the top part of the shoe, cut and stitched
vocabulary.lasting: shaping the upper over a last and attaching it
vocabulary.last: foot-shaped form a shoe is built on
vocabulary.size set / size run: the mix of sizes in a production lot or carton
vocabulary.moulds: dies for soles, size-specific and costly
vocabulary.pairs: the unit output is counted in
vocabulary.khussa/ chappal: traditional embroidered shoe / slipper or sandal

problems.phrase: We have size 40 and 41 stuck while 42 and 43 sold out
Size sets get broken at the godown and dealers refuse half sets
Sole supplier delivers late and lasting stops
We don’t have moulds in all sizes so some sizes can’t be made
Mould or press breaks and we lose days
Old articles stay in stock for seasons
Dealers return shoes after the season
Sole separation complaints coming back
Defects found only when dealers open cartons
Dealers take goods on credit and pay after the season
Cash is stuck in stock and receivables at the same time
PU and chemicals keep getting expensive
We don’t know cost per pair for each article
Pairs per worker are disputed every week (piece rate)
Skilled lasting and closing workers keep switching factories
School shoe season order rush overwhelms us
Own shops’ sales aren’t visible to the factory until month end
Shop counts of pairs never match what we dispatched
Daraz orders come in with the wrong size picked
Online returns for size are high
Designs are copied by others in the market within weeks
Leftover leather and synthetic pieces walk out
No planning for which articles to make next season
Production updates are on WhatsApp voice notes

stock: Which sizes or articles get stuck most?
How do you see stock by size today?
size sets: How are cartons packed — full size sets or loose pairs?
materials: Which material stops production most — soles, uppers, adhesive or packing?
How much warning do you get?
moulds and machines: Do you have moulds for every size you sell?
quality: What do customers return shoes for most?
Is there a check before cartons are closed?
dealers: How many active dealers do you supply?
What credit period do they usually take?
returns: How much comes back after the season?
costing: How do you work out cost per pair?
staff: Are workers paid per pair, per day or monthly?
seasons: Which season is biggest for you?
How early do you start producing for it?
own retail and online: Do you have your own shops or sell online?
How quickly do you see what’s sold there?

seasons: Pakistan: Eid ul Fitr is the biggest footwear season by far, with heavy pre-Eid production and dealer orders weeks ahead; Eid ul Adha a second peak; school shoes in March to April (new session) and August; wedding season (roughly October to March) for formal and khussa; winter boots and closed shoes from October; summer chappals and sandals from March. UAE: back-to-school (late August), Ramadan and Eid, Dubai Shopping Festival, summer slowdown. Canada: back-to-school, winter boots (October to January), spring/summer sandals, Black Friday and Boxing Day.
care: Fumes from adhesives or solvents causing collapse, fires, machine injuries: pi stops and points to emergency services.
No advice on safety-footwear certification, standards or how to claim them; no medical or orthopaedic claims.
No help copying another brand’s trademarks or logos, or making counterfeit goods; pi declines plainly.
No customs, tax or under-invoicing help.
Never stores dealer, worker or customer personal details; uses roles like “Lahore dealer” or “lasting worker”.
Piece-rate disputes: pi notes the counting gap, does not judge fairness or wage legality.
build_ideas: Article-size matrix stock: pairs by article, colour and size across factory, godown and shops.
Size-set carton packing with scan-in/scan-out to stop broken sets.
Production lot tracker through cutting, closing, lasting, finishing, with pairs per stage.
Mould register by article and size, with condition and repair history.
Material requirement from planned pairs (soles, uppers, adhesive, boxes) with shortage alerts.
Dealer ordering via WhatsApp catalogue with size-set selection and credit limit checks.
Dealer ledger with ageing and season-end return tracking.
Pre-dispatch QC checklist with defect types and photos.
Piece-count capture per worker per day, feeding a weekly wage sheet.
Cost per pair calculator by article using current material rates.
Own-shop sales sync to the factory daily, with size-level sell-through.
Season planning view comparing last season’s sales by article and size.

exchange.text: Eid ke liye maal banaya, ab 40-41 size pada hai aur 43 ki demand hai jo khatam ho gaya.
Samajh gaya, noted: Eid stock mein chhote size bach gaye aur bade size khatam. Production ke waqt size ka mix kaise decide hota hai?
Pichle saal ke andaaze se, likha hua kuch nahi.
Noted, size mix andaaze se banta hai, record nahi hai. Dealers ko aap full size set mein dete hain ya woh apni marzi ke size chunte hain?
Set mein, lekin woh set tod dete hain.
Noted, dealers set tod dete hain. Jo pairs bach jaate hain, woh season ke baad wapas aate hain ya dealers ke paas pade rehte hain?
